Betty Ketani's Murder Follow UP

By: Diana Lucas | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
An extraordinary murder is solved.

Summary:
The story behind Betty Ketani’s murder reads like a film script with twists and turns at every point, Carte Blanche covered the story around a year ago when the court case was ongoing and fascinating the public. In May the accused will be sentenced, we reconnect with the story and the result of one of South Africa’s prime investigations. Alex Eliseev, senior EWN reporter, has been following the case and in May will publish a book on the Ketani murder.

Further information:
The story behind Betty Ketani’s murder reads like a film script with twists and turns at every point, Carte Blanche covered the story around a year ago when the court case was ongoing and fascinating the public. In May the accused will be sentenced, we reconnect with the story and the result of one of South Africa’s prime investigations. Alex Eliseev, senior EWN reporter, has been following the case and in May will publish a book on the Ketani murder.
In 1999, 37 year old Betty Ketani, a chef at the colourful Johannesburg restaurant Cranks, went missing without a trace. Betty was from the Eastern Cape but worked in Johannesburg and sent money home to her 3 children in Queenstown. The youngest was 7 months old at the time of her disappearance in 1999. 13 years later, a written confession was found hidden beneath the carpets at a house in Kenilworth Werner Nortje found the confession letter when he and his then fiancé were renovating the house they’d rented out for 10 years to a man called Conway Brown. The letter of confession suggests that Cranks was connected to Betty’s disappearance. The owner, Eric Neetesen-Lemkes, was of Dutch descent. Better known to some as Mad Dog Eric. His daughter Monique alos worked at Cranks, handling accounts and customer service. The names ‘Monique’ and ‘Cranks’ appear in the confession letter, suggesting some connection to the disappearance of chef Betty Ketani. Cranks closed its doors in 2012, just weeks after the arrest of the six men named in the confession letter. And Monique returned to Australia shortly after Betty disappeared.
The typed confession starts with: ‘ Contained here is all the information relating to Monique and the investigation that was undertaken. As well as the details of those concerned and the level of their involvement. Your mission is to bring them all down, completely’. Former private investigator Carrington Laughton has been accused of kidnapping and murdering Betty Ketani. When Betty disappeared, he was in a relationship with Monique Neetesen-Lemkes. Carrington was alleged to have written the confession letter. But he said it was a forgery. So why would anyone have written it and hidden it? Brothers and former cops, Carel and David Ranger also stood accused of Betty’s kidnapping and murder. Named as co-conspirators were Monique Neetesen-Lemkes and a man called Mark Lister, who also lives in Australia. Both have been issued with an arrest warrant and placed on Interpol’s Red Notice.
Three of the six accused turned state-witnesses. They are Paul Toft-Nielsen, Dirk Reinecke and Conway Brown.
The big question is Why…why was Betty Ketani murdered? Did there begin to be an issue of concern that money was going missing in the business..EWN reporter, Alex Eliseev broke the story in 2012. He has followed every step of this cold case and is writing a book on it.
Carrington Laughton, Carel Ranger and David Ranger are on trial at the South Gauteng High Court, which is sitting at the Palm Ridge Magistrate Court.

Betty Ketani was a breadwinner. She worked in Johannesburg and sent money home every month. Her disappearance had an emotional and financial impact on her family here in the Eastern Cape.
The story behind Betty Ketani’s murder reads like a film script with twists and turns at every point, Carte Blanche covered the story around a year ago when the court case was ongoing and fascinating the public. In May the accused will be sentenced, we reconnect with the story and the result of one of South Africa’s prime investigations. Alex Eliseev, senior EWN reporter, has been following the case and in May will publish a book on the Ketani murder.

Press Release:


Betty Ketani
Soon after Betty Ketani was murdered in 1999 clues about what happened to the mother of three dried up. Fifteen long years later, a confession letter was discovered beginning with the words, “If you are reading this then I am dead”. The letter revealed her fate and more. For Betty Ketani’s family it’s been almost two decades of waiting for closure. Her killers are now behind bars, but many questions remain. Carte Blanche reports on a sizzling legal battle and a narrative matched by few Hollywood thrillers.


Script:


V/O
Early Thursday morning, the family of murdered Betty Ketani made their way from their home, Queenstown in the Eastern Cape to Johannesburg, With them they brought an empty coffin and a thorn branch to perform a ritual that they believe will finally let her soul rest in peace.

LINK
According to Xhosa tradition the Ketani Family has to come here to this abandoned bus where its believed BK live her last few hours here they have to beg her soul ask her soul to beg her soul to come back to their home in the Eastern case.

Mankinki, : We was just calling my sister, my sister come come to us must go Queenstown with us you mustn’t just lie there in that bus you must be at home, take that spirit know with us.

V/O
On Friday the 6th May/ Last week, after four years, 97 day days in court and 46 witnesses….three of Betty Ketani’ s convicted killers were sentenced.

V/O
For the investigating officer Capt. Gerhard Van Wyk its been years of dogged foot work.

Gerhard speaks re family
Very relieved for the family to eventually get closure that’s the best I could do for the family……its simple its my job that’s what the community expect of you to do the job to the beat of your ability,

V/O
Carrington Laughton was sentenced to 30 years in jail for kidnapping, attempted murder and murder… the two policeman brothers Carel and David Ranger ,4 years each for their role in helping kidnap Betty Ketani. Leave to appeal was refused.

Herman: This is one of those one in a life time cases where you’ve got no body.

V/O
For Lead prosecutor Advocate Herman Broodryk this is the most difficult case he has ever prosecuted in his 34 year career.

Herman: To prove a case without the body is an almost an insurmountable onus which is placed on the state and that was the challenge

Link
Betty Ketani was murdered 17 years ago, but the murder literally lay buried until 4 years ago when a letter was found under a carpet in a home in Johannesburg. The letter revealed an incredible confession, a secret lying fallow for years.

V/O
Betty was the chef of a crazy Thai restaurant called Cranks in Johannesburg. Cranks was owned and run by Eric Neetesen- Lemkes and his daughter Monique…

Alex Everybody wants to know but why would this cook this lady….mother of the three who came up from the Eastern Cape why would she be murdered.

V/O 5 sec
It was Alex Eliseev, reporter for Eye Witness News who first broke the story in 2012.

Alex 01 43 36 Right from the wante to see through…honour for a jo…parachuting in and out

Link
When Betty disappeared in May 1999, her family back in the Eastern Cape had no idea what had happened. She had three daughters one who was only a few months old. Betty was the sole breadwinner… desperate to find their mother or at least what happened to her, the family came to Johannesburg.

Alex: In 2012 when the confession was found the family were still hoping to see Betty Ketani walk through the door one day they refused to believe she was dead the older children thought that she could have been kidnapped because they never believed for a second that she would have just left her children> …

BETTY KETANI’S DAUGHTER The last time I saw her was Easter 1999. But I knew she hadn’t abandoned us, because she loved us. For us to grow up without a mother is a painful thing.

Link
The letter opened a hornets nest a murder with twists at every turn, unanswered questions … reading like a Holly wood whodunit.

V/O
It was signed by Carrington Laughton, who had been working for Cranks as a private investigator, but Carrington maintained the letter was forged…

Herman: Without that confession letter there was nothing this is a version given by the accused from his own mouth.
Devi: But then he said it’s not true?
Herman That’s ok we knew we could prove that this is not only a confession that you are lucky to find it was a typed out confession signed by him and signed on every page so it was a very important piece of evidence.
V/O
The letter vividly described how Carrington and his friend Conway Brown had attacked Betty in the middle of the night leaving her for dead on a deserted road…….But Betty did not die,

Herman She did not die she landed up In K H we don’t know how we just have word of the accused in that regard,

V/O
The big break came when Carrington’s friend and accomplice to the murder Conway Brown confessed…. Then they had names of the role players in the crime and arrests rolled out..

Three of the men arrested, Conway Brown, Paul Toft Nielson and Dirk Reinecke pleaded guilty and turned state witness’s.

Evidence in court described how Carrington and the Ranger brothers abducted Betty from the Hospital

01 12 10 How did they do that
That’s the theory that’s why accused no 2 and 3 had to go along to assist in that regard, but Carrington said in his statement they were dressed as medical personnel we don’t know.
Herman: Once she was kidnapped she was taken to a remote little plot near Kliprivier there she was placed in an old railways bus ///and there she must have died they put her the but we don’t know if she was assaulted or she died of over exposure it was the 12th June it was the middle of the winter it was cold.

V/O
Betty;s body was buried in Conway’s back yard ….and covered with cement

Herman: Then after ¾ years we are not exactly for some reason or another Carrington, something must have happened to cause him to get Conway Brown and another friend of his Paul Toft Nielson to go and dig up the body and get rid of it
IN COURT TESTIMONY – PAUL TOFT-NIELSEN We started to open the concrete and the smell was terrible.
IN COURT TESTIMONY – PAUL TOFT-NIELSEN We then started disposing of the remains by lowering the packets into the water.. I put the skull on the ground and smacked it with a small hammer. I put that into the water first and then emptied the rest of the contents of the bag.
BULELWA KETANI – BETTY’S DAUGHTER She was buried like she wasn’t a human being.

LINK
The two legs the success of the investigation rested one were the handwriting analysis, which convinced Judge Ranchod that the confession letter was in fact written by accused number 1 ,Carrington Laughton and the DNA proof that six tiny bones dug up in the original grave were linked to the Ketani family

Herman: The first 2 excavations did not yield anything but then we got in the real experts from Pretoria from the Victim Identification Centre and they excavated it again the proper way and then they uncovered six small pieces of bones. Very very small like the tips of your fingers or the tips of your toes

V/O
Local labs were battling to get the DNA out of the bones so the bones were sent to the Bosnia International Commission of missing people. After months they managed to drew out a DNA sample that linked the bones to Betty’s children’s DNA.

Herman: Now you had corroboration that that was `BK bones which were found there in that yard pointed out by a co accused… very important piece of circumstantial evidence.

Alex: And Once all that came together what you had was these strands of circumstantial evidence independently they have been perhaps to weak to hang a conviction on but tie them all together in this thick strong tope and that s where the court found that there was enough evidence to give the conviction.

V/O 8 sec
The elements of this investigation and case have resulted in Alex writing a book.

Alex: You simply cannot make this stuff up its impossible to make up if you look at the characters the names the plot twists its amazing to think things happen out there. We live our lives we think nothing goes on….

Devi Why was she murdered
Herman I think that is one of the great mysteries even in the sentence proceedings the presiding judge stated the deceased was killed for reasons that remain unknown.

Alex:
there’s a lot of speculation she may have know something that somebody didn’t want her to know she may have found out something, she may have been killed by an interrogation that went wrong we simply don’t know because the people who have been convicted for this crime still maintain that they are ab innocent and they have been framed for murder.

V/O
V/O
And suspect Monique, Neetesen- Lemkes, whose name has been linked to the murder, has not yet been tried. When the investigation began Cranks closed its doors and Monique and her father Eric left the country.

Herman :I don’t think it’s a secret that throughout the trial we have said that we are going to apply for extradition but as to the facts of that I would not like to elaborate because obviously that is sub-judice.
.
Devi What does it feel like
Herman: You know after the conviction I walked out of court and I saw Bulewaya the eldest and I said its over and its done and I looked into her eyes and she was crying and thought to myself of all the heart ache and hardship and suffering in this case // it completely pales into insignificance if you look at her and you see the grief in her eyes and I wish I could do more I wish I could get you a body but I cannot for everybody you want a grave you can visit whatever your cultural beliefs are there must be a place to go// they don’t have a place like that// that is the satisfaction in a case like this not successful, no that you managed to get them behind bars but that you gave some sort of closure….

V/O
Whilst Betty died in a bus ….her body was buried in a back yard in the Kennilworth Johannesburg …and its here the family continue their lonely and sad procession to take the soil from her burial site

V/O
It is all finally to much for the children of Betty Ketani

V/O
And also Mankinki, who remembers his parents who died without knowing what happened to their daughter.

Makinki: Before my mother is dead they must know where the bones are… is painful my mum is lying there she know nothing about his daughter…that is very important.

Lusanda: It was not easy for me today was very painful for me but I am happy to my mother to have finally found closure and family.

V/O Whilst Betty died in a bus ….her body was buried in a back yard in the Kennilworth Johannesburg …and its here the family continue their lonely and sad procession to take the soil from her burial site V/O It is all finally to much for the children of Betty Ketani V/O And also Mankinki, who remembers his parents who died without knowing what happened to their daughter. Makinki: Before my mother is dead they must know where the bones are… is painful my mum is lying there she know nothing about his daughter…that is very important. Lusanda: It was not easy for me today was very painful for me but I am happy to my mother to have finally found closure and family.

metadata.Further information: The story behind Betty Ketani’s murder reads like a film script with twists and turns at every point, Carte Blanche covered the story around a year ago when the court case was ongoing and fascinating the public. In May the accused will be sentenced, we reconnect with the story and the result of one of South Africa’s prime investigations. Alex Eliseev, senior EWN reporter, has been following the case and in May will publish a book on the Ketani murder. In 1999, 37 year old Betty Ketani, a chef at the colourful Johannesburg restaurant Cranks, went missing without a trace. Betty was from the Eastern Cape but worked in Johannesburg and sent money home to her 3 children in Queenstown. The youngest was 7 months old at the time of her disappearance in 1999. 13 years later, a written confession was found hidden beneath the carpets at a house in Kenilworth Werner Nortje found the confession letter when he and his then fiancé were renovating the house they’d rented out for 10 years to a man called Conway Brown. The letter of confession suggests that Cranks was connected to Betty’s disappearance. The owner, Eric Neetesen-Lemkes, was of Dutch descent. Better known to some as Mad Dog Eric. His daughter Monique alos worked at Cranks, handling accounts and customer service. The names ‘Monique’ and ‘Cranks’ appear in the confession letter, suggesting some connection to the disappearance of chef Betty Ketani. Cranks closed its doors in 2012, just weeks after the arrest of the six men named in the confession letter. And Monique returned to Australia shortly after Betty disappeared. The typed confession starts with: ‘ Contained here is all the information relating to Monique and the investigation that was undertaken. As well as the details of those concerned and the level of their involvement. Your mission is to bring them all down, completely’. Former private investigator Carrington Laughton has been accused of kidnapping and murdering Betty Ketani. When Betty disappeared, he was in a relationship with Monique Neetesen-Lemkes. Carrington was alleged to have written the confession letter. But he said it was a forgery. So why would anyone have written it and hidden it? Brothers and former cops, Carel and David Ranger also stood accused of Betty’s kidnapping and murder. Named as co-conspirators were Monique Neetesen-Lemkes and a man called Mark Lister, who also lives in Australia. Both have been issued with an arrest warrant and placed on Interpol’s Red Notice. Three of the six accused turned state-witnesses. They are Paul Toft-Nielsen, Dirk Reinecke and Conway Brown. The big question is Why…why was Betty Ketani murdered? Did there begin to be an issue of concern that money was going missing in the business..EWN reporter, Alex Eliseev broke the story in 2012. He has followed every step of this cold case and is writing a book on it. Carrington Laughton, Carel Ranger and David Ranger are on trial at the South Gauteng High Court, which is sitting at the Palm Ridge Magistrate Court. Betty Ketani was a breadwinner. She worked in Johannesburg and sent money home every month. Her disappearance had an emotional and financial impact on her family here in the Eastern Cape. The story behind Betty Ketani’s murder reads like a film script with twists and turns at every point, Carte Blanche covered the story around a year ago when the court case was ongoing and fascinating the public.
